v0.0.3.8 (2026-10-13) [testing]

- The BossMod preset named "Gluttony" that earlier versions created is no longer used. It is left untouched in BossMod's preset list and can be deleted there by hand.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Click behavior, the confirming second click and every other part of the server bar entry are unchanged.

v0.0.3.6 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The server info bar entry shows the boss FATE icon instead of the sword glyphs.** The same icon is used in every state; the bot's on/off state stays in the text (": On", ": Off" and the rest), exactly as before. No other entry is affected.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- The click behavior, the confirming second click and everything else in the previous build are unchanged.

v0.0.3.5 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **Server info bar (Umbra) toggle for the FATE bot.** The plugin adds a "Lazy Fate Automation" entry to the game's server info bar, which Umbra renders as a button. It shows the bot state with the sibling entries' sword icon: On, Off, "(stopping)" while a soft stop is pending, or the live state such as "Paused (in instance)". Clicking it stops the bot (Ctrl+click waits for the current FATE to finish, like the window's soft stop); when stopped, the first click arms the start and a second click within 10 seconds confirms it, so a stray click cannot start the automation. Starting still requires a logged-in character, exactly like the Lazy Hub switch.
- New display setting "Show server info bar entry" (on by default) hides or shows the entry; it can also be hidden per-plugin in Umbra or under /xlsettings -> Server Info Bar.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

{"Author":"GitHixy","Name":"HitSpark","Punchline":"Replace the game's combat numbers with animated, styleable fly text.","Description":"HitSpark replaces Final Fantasy XIV's combat text with its own renderer: better fonts, tuned motion and real impact on critical hits.

WHAT YOU GET

- Every kind of combat text redrawn: damage dealt and taken, healing, misses and evades, status effects, experience, crafting and loot.
- Eight built-in presets, each a complete look: Classic+, Heroic, Tally, Onslaught, Elemental, Grim, Minimal and Retro.
- Real motion: arcs, fountains, rising and falling paths, scrolling columns, and punch, shake, flash, sparks and trails on crits.
- Multi-hits and damage over time that roll up into one number, with DoT ticks in their own colour.
- Other players' numbers shown smaller, or hidden, for your party and for everyone else.
- A style editor for every category with a live preview, and presets you can share as a short code.

GETTING STARTED

Type /hitspark (or /hs) to open the settings and pick a preset. /hitspark test plays sample numbers on you and your target, even out of combat.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you.

PLAYS BY THE RULES

HitSpark is purely cosmetic: it only redraws text the game already shows you and follows the game's own flying text and pop-up text options. {"Author":"GitHixy","Name":"FateLimit","Punchline":"See the edge of every FATE, and know before you step out of it.","Description":"FateLimit draws the border of FATE areas right in the world, so you always know where the fight ends and never lose your level sync by wandering out.

WHAT YOU GET

- Five border styles made to sit in Eorzea: Aether ring, Barrier wall, Marching dashes, Crystal runes and FATE ember.
- Two ways to show them: always, or only when you get close to the edge of the FATE you're in.
- A warning colour that creeps in as you near the edge, an on-screen banner with the distance left and a marker on the closest point of the border.
- Borders that follow the ground over hills and slopes instead of floating through them.
- Colour, thickness, height, spacing, glow and animation for every style, with a live preview in the settings.

GETTING STARTED

Type /fatelimit (or /fl) to open the settings. /fatelimit test places a practice FATE around you so you can try every style without waiting for a real one.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you, or come and talk about it on Discord: https://discord.gg/9kjUjWDBkJ

PLAYS BY THE RULES

FateLimit is purely visual: it only reads where FATEs are, which the game already shows on your map, and draws over the screen. It never moves your character or sends anything to the game. Settings are stored locally and nothing is ever uploaded.","Changelog":"# Version 0.1.0

{"Author":"DhogGPT","Name":"Deep Ducking","Punchline":"Deep Ducking public host and authenticated module access.","Description":"The Deep Ducking public host provides the introduction, community links and authenticated loading of separately supplied DDuck modules. /deepducking and /dduck open the introduction when no module is loaded.

Commands (use /deepducking; /dduck is an alias):
/deepducking [toggle main window]
/dduck [alias for /deepducking; accepts all commands below]
/deepducking mini [toggle Mini]
/deepducking settings [open Settings]
/deepducking config [open Settings]
/deepducking debug [reveal and open Advanced for this plugin load]
/deepducking help [open command help]
/deepducking start [floor] [start or continue selected save; optional fresh-run floor]
/deepducking party-start [floor] [alias for start]
/deepducking party [select fixed-party POTD while idle]
/deepducking adopt [bind eligible already-entered party dungeon]
/deepducking hold [pause local output; retain run for Resume]
/deepducking resume [resume retained local run after readiness checks]
/deepducking nextstop [exit after next boss]
/deepducking ns [exit after next boss]
/deepducking stop [FULL STOP; persist local lock across reloads; stay in duty]
/deepducking reset-stop [clear eligible FULL STOP after cleanup; do not start]
/deepducking status [print local status]
/deepducking inspect [record read-only client and native observations]
/deepducking saves [open Saves]
/deepducking saves info <dungeon> [inspect native saves]
/deepducking saves delete <dungeon> <1|2> [delete selected save after native checks; no extra confirmation]
/deepducking saves dof <dungeon> <1|2> <on|off> [set future-failure deletion preference; no deletion now]
/deepducking saves cancel [cancel pending save or Start preparation; completed actions remain]

Dungeon arguments: potd, hoh, eo, pt. [floor] is optional; <...> is required. Choose one value for 1|2 or on|off; omit brackets when typing. Start can replace stopped state; Resume can release an eligible retained in-dungeon run. nextstop and ns retain the save and keep Mini open until return is observed; repeat to confirm the same request.
